prompt: Put the phases of one trading day in the order described in this chapter. Exact times are not part of this question.

options.text: Pre-open (orders collected, opening price worked out)

explanations.a: Correct position: last. The closing session sets the closing price at the end of the day.
explanations.b: Correct position: first. Pre-open collects orders and works out the opening price before continuous trading starts.
explanations.c: Correct position: middle. Continuous trading matches orders as they arrive, between the pre-open and the closing session.

prompt: Your plan is written on Friday after the close. Monday is a made-up holiday, so the next session is Tuesday. How many calendar days are there from Friday to Tuesday?
solution: Count the days after Friday: Saturday (1), Sunday (2), Monday (3), Tuesday (4). Answer: 4 calendar days. Only Tuesday is a trading day in that span, because Saturday and Sunday are weekends and Monday is a holiday.

prompt: A reader says: 'I can trade on Saturday, because I have a free day and my broker app is open.' Which statement is correct?

options.text: Yes. If the broker app is open, the exchange matches orders on Saturday.
No. Weekends are non-trading days. An order placed then is handled under the broker and exchange rules and waits for a trading session.
Yes, Saturday is always a special session.
Only when a holiday falls on a Saturday.

explanations.a: Wrong. An open broker app does not mean the exchange is trading. The exchange matches orders only in its trading sessions.
explanations.c: Wrong. The exchange announces special sessions for specific days. A normal Saturday is not one of them.
explanations.d: Wrong. Holidays remove trading days. They do not create trading on weekends.

prompt: A reader says: 'The pre-open price is the closing price, so I can plan from it.' Which part of this statement is wrong?

options.text: 'The pre-open price' is wrong. Pre-open is a phase, not a price.
'Is the closing price' is wrong. The pre-open price is set in the pre-open phase, and the closing price is set in the closing session. They are different phases.

explanations.a: Wrong. Pre-open is the phase where orders are collected and an opening price is worked out. The term is correct.
explanations.c: Wrong. The pre-open price and the closing price come from different phases of the day, so they are not the same thing.

prompt: A swing trader places a stop-loss based on Friday's close, before a long weekend that includes a made-up Monday holiday. Which risk is the main one to plan for?

options.text: No risk. A stop always fills at the stop price, even if the price gaps.
Gap risk. The next session can open far from the stop price, so the fill can be worse than planned.
The stop cannot be placed before a holiday, so the trader has no protection.

explanations.a: Wrong. A stop is a trigger, and the fill can be at a worse price when the market gaps. The chapter on stop-loss orders explains this.
explanations.c: Wrong. Whether a stop can be placed at a given time depends on broker and exchange rules. The main risk is the gap at the next open.
